description: Klipper pipetting robot deck. Machine envelope, slot centres, fixed stations and keep-out zones.

conventions.z_note: Z=0 is home/top. LARGER Z is LOWER. A move from Z145 to Z137 is 8 mm UP.
conventions.xy_order: X first, then Y. Never diagonal. Enforced by the library.

x.note: homes at 420 and counts down toward 0

z.note: kinematic limit only; the real limit is effector-dependent, see simulate.py

z.travel_note: 5.0. Now verified rather than assumed: with a 300 uL tip fitted this clears the raised location edges by 48.0 mm and the stage floor by 57.5 mm.
z.stage_surface_note: Z at which a BARE p300 nosecone contacts the main stage. Measured 2026-08-26. This is the bare-nosecone reference every other Z limit is derived from.
z.stage_surface_with_p300_tip_note: Same stage, with a 300 uL tip fitted. Measured 2026-08-26. The difference 114.75 - 62.5 = 52.25 mm IS the tip length, and that is where labware.json tiprack_300_96.tip.length comes from - it is derived, not independently guessed.
z.slot_edge_note: The edges of each stage location are raised. With a 300 uL tip fitted, Z must be 53.0 or LOWER (i.e. physically higher) whenever the effector moves across a location corner, or the tip strikes an edge piece. Measured 2026-08-26. Bare-nosecone equivalent is 53.0 + 52.25 = 105.25, so the edges stand 62.5 - 53.0 = 9.5 mm above the stage floor. This limit applies to motion that CROSSES a location boundary; motion staying inside one location (the wall wipe, which works inside a tube) is not over an edge.
z.stage_region_note: The stage surface only exists over the slot area, derived in code as the slot centres expanded by half the slot pitch. Off-stage the surface limit does not apply, which is what makes the ejector's Z 145 reachable - it hangs past the front of the stage. Deck.point_on_stage() is the test; the simulator asserts the ejector really is off-stage rather than taking it on trust.
z.stage_surface_reference_note: Which effector's BARE nosecone the 114.75 was measured with. A different pipette body sits at a different height, so this reference does not transfer automatically. The simulator warns when the loaded effector is not this one.

slot_frame.note: Machine X = 420 + stored. parameters.json stored slot X as negative (-84/-220/-355). Confirmed by three labware landing on the slots the operator names, once the +70 frame shift is applied to the pre-shift coordinates - see coordinate_frame.

slot_order_note: Row-major. Slots 1-3 are the FRONT row (largest Y, 365), 4-6 the middle row (272), 7-9 the BACK row (smallest Y, 178.5). Within each row X descends: the first of the three is highest X. Operator-confirmed 2026-08-26.
slot_pitch_note: X pitch is 136/135 and Y pitch is 93.0/93.5 - irregular by ~1 mm. Per-slot centres are stored rather than derived from a pitch so the irregularity survives. Unverified whether it is a real measured frame or transcription drift.

water.z_note: submerge depth is per-effector, see effectors/*.json -> z_for_labware.reservoir_water.work
water.frame_note: was X 0 in the pre-shift frame; +70 applied

park.frame_note: was X 350 in the pre-shift frame; +70 applied. 420 is X home, which is what this station always meant.

tip_eject.description: tip ejector lane. Operator-confirmed 2026-08-25: the working lane is X 155 (supersedes an earlier X 85 note).
tip_eject.strip_note: Z145 -> Z137 is an 8 mm UPWARD stroke because +Z is down. That is the strip.
tip_eject.rehome_note: The strip force can skip steps on an open-loop machine, so commanded position is untrustworthy afterward. G28 is mandatory, not optional.
tip_eject.validated_note: NEVER RUN ON HARDWARE UNVALIDATED. No existing gcode file in this repo contains an ejection sequence; this routine has no working reference. Dry-run it, then step through manually at reduced feedrate.
tip_eject.frame_note: X 155 was measured AFTER the +70 X limit change, so it is already in the current frame and needs no correction. Operator-confirmed 2026-08-26.

keepouts.description: Y-axis motion inside this X band collides with the ejector mechanism unless the effector is ABOVE Z 60 (i.e. commanded Z < 60).
keepouts.x_range_note: Derived as the ejector lane X 155 +/- 7.0, current frame (the lane was measured after the +70 X limit change). The 14 mm width is carried over from the previously documented band centred on X 85 and is still UNVERIFIED at this location - measure the mechanism width and correct x_range if it differs. x_range is the single source of truth.
keepouts.safe_when_z_below_note: Stated for the 300 uL effector with NO TIP. With a tip fitted the effector reaches lower and the safe Z shrinks. tip_length is unmeasured, so any TIPPED Y-traverse through this band is treated as an error.

temperature_sensors.note: section names must match printer.cfg exactly

uncalibrated: keepouts.tip_ejector.x_range (width unverified; lane X 155 itself is confirmed and post-shift)

coordinate_frame.description: The X travel limit was increased by 70 mm. The machine homes at max X, so the same physical endstop is now called 420 where it used to be 350, and every physical point gained 70 in X. Coordinates written before that change are 70 mm too low in the current frame and have been corrected here.
evidence: tube rack grid centre 132 + 70 = 202 vs slot 8 at 200 (2.0 mm) - the estimate that established the shift; direct measurement later put the grid centre at 202.6, 4.8 mm from the slot centre, which is a better seating and corroborates the shift rather than revising it
water dip point 0 + 70 = 70 vs slot 9 at 65 (5.0 mm)
park 350 + 70 = 420 = X home exactly; park at X350 in a 0-350 machine WAS 'go to X home', which only makes sense if 350 was the old maximum
the tube rack unshifted (X 78-186) straddles the slot 8/9 cell seam at 132.25 and is seated in neither; shifted (X 148-256) it fits entirely inside slot 8, which is where the operator says it is
the tip rack measured at X 68 after the change matches slot 3 at 65 with no shift, confirming the measurement is already in the current frame
corrected: layout tubes anchor_xy X 186 -> 256 (later superseded by direct measurement, see superseded_by_measurement)
unaffected: all Y coordinates - only the X limit changed
the tip rack corners - measured after the change
the tip ejector lane X 155 - operator states this as current
coordinate_frame.why_it_went_unnoticed: The tube column pitch is 12.0 mm and the frame error was 70.0 mm = 6 columns minus 2.0 mm. A shifted well therefore lands 2.0 mm from a REAL well centre, well inside a ~8 mm tube. Running pre-shift gcode today would have dispensed into actual tubes six columns from the intended ones - no crash, no visible sign, and since row = volume and column = replicate, every volume would have landed in the wrong replicate set while the balance readings still looked plausible. Verify frames with tools/check_alignment.py, not by eye.
coordinate_frame.verification: tools/check_alignment.py --shift 70 on the three committed pre-shift gcode files resolves every working position onto the current deck. The single exception is the old tip station (218, 309) -> (288, 309), which is slot 4 where the PREVIOUS tip rack sat and where nothing is loaded now.
coordinate_frame.superseded_by_measurement: The tube rack anchor is no longer a shifted old value. The operator measured the centre of well A1 directly on 2026-08-27 as (256.6, 218.5), so layout.json now carries that. Relative to the old script constant (186, 223) the total delta is (+70.6, -4.5), but the FRAME SHIFT IS STILL EXACTLY 70 - the extra (+0.6, -4.5) is measurement correcting an estimate, not a different frame. Do not infer a 70.6 mm shift from the anchor.
